title: Stale Vector3i typing in tscn causes it to revert to default Vector3 in exported build only
body: ### Tested versions Tested in v4.7.1.stable.official [a13da4feb] ### System information Godot v4.7.1.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8228) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-7700HQ CPU @ 2.80GHz (8 threads) - 15.86 GiB memory - Dummy (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description I had a number of scenes with a script with a Vector3i `@export` variable. I later changed it to be a Vector3, but didn't go back and re-save all the scenes that were using that script to update the tscn values. When run from the editor, the old Vector3i is automatically converted to a Vector3 and the scenes still work correctly: However, if you export and run the project, the `@export`ed Vector3i values are ignored and it reverts to the default value in the class: This one's on me for not re-saving all my scenes after changing the vector type, but I'm making a report here because it's a hard-to-notice, bug-in-exported-build-only issue. I don't have an opinion on which direction it should be fixed (editor ignores stale Vector3i value or export is also able to automatically convert Vector3i -> Vector3) but it should be the same for either method of running the game. ### Steps to reproduce [Important: don't open node_3d.tscn in the editor and re-save it; the bug only shows up when it has stale Vector3i typing] 1. Run the project in the editor. See that the windmill tines spin in the expected direction. 2. Export the project without changing anything. 3. Run the exported project. See that the windmill tines spin in a different direction. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [rotating-mesh.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31147235/rotating-mesh.zip)
